headers.//: Vercel's default for a static file is max-age=0, must-revalidate: every asset costs a round trip on every visit, and on cellular that latency is most of what a repeat visitor waits for even though almost nothing comes back. stale-while-revalidate hands over the cached copy at once and checks behind it, so the second visit paints immediately. Bounded on purpose — an hour fresh, a day stale at worst — rather than the year you would use if these filenames carried a content hash. They do not: there is no build step to add one, so a long cache would mean a replaced picture staying replaced for nobody. Only assets/, because js/ and css/ have to stay in step with the html that loads them, and html itself must never be stale or a deploy is invisible.
